question: Do official CvSU project and research-newsletter records reveal fish-sampling deliverables for the Imus River Watershed project?

sourceReviews.title: Bio-physical Characterization, Vulnerability and Pollution Assessment in Imus River Watershed

findings.catalogPeriod: The Research Center listing gives NOV. 2020–APR. 2021 and identifies Prof. Noel A. Sedigo, CAFENR, and PEMSEA funding.
findings.presentationCrossCheck: The opened page shows this Imus entry at row 63. A separate row 60 is an unrelated emerging-energy project; do not merge its coauthors or DOE funding with the Imus project.
findings.fishEvidence: The project-listing row gives no fish methods, sites, taxa, dataset, or report link.

sourceReviews.title: CvSU collaborates with NIVA, PEMSEA, DLSU-D on ASEANO project
sourceReviews.provider: CvSU Office of the Vice President for Research and Extension newsletter

findings.projectPeriodAsReported: The newsletter says the PEMSEA-funded project was approved in November 2020 and was planned to run in Cavite from January through June 2021, differing from the Research Center listing’s November 2020–April 2021 period.
findings.statedScope: The summary describes planned GIS/remote-sensing watershed mapping and characterization, maps of physical and demographic/climate context, plastic-source/pathway mapping, and plastic-pollution hotspot analysis. It names DLSU-D and CvSU project roles.
findings.fishEvidence: The searchable newsletter text contains no fish taxa, fish-sampling method, fish station, or fish results. This does not prove that no fish work occurred in the full project.

sourceReviews.title: CvSU research and extension forum project results
sourceReviews.provider: CvSU Office of the Vice President for Research and Extension newsletter

findings.outcome: The September 2022 newsletter lists the Imus watershed project among Natural and Life Science research projects recognized at the CvSU Research and Extension forum; it identifies Prof. Noel A. Sedigo and additional CvSU collaborators.
findings.fishEvidence: The reported forum recognition is a project-outcome lead, not a published fish checklist. The searchable newsletter text does not provide fish taxa, stations, methods, or occurrence dates.

reconciliation.projectIdentity: The official listing and the two CvSU newsletters share the Imus watershed project and PEMSEA context, but the project-period descriptions differ and should remain source-specific until the final report resolves them.
reconciliation.scope: Public summaries point to watershed characterization and plastic-pollution work. They do not disclose enough to determine whether the complete project collected fish data.
reconciliation.access: No final report, fish-data table, station list, or downloadable dataset was located in this follow-up. Continue through authorized repository/library routes.

rightsReview.decision: Keep bibliographic metadata and short factual research notes only. Do not copy newsletter prose, maps, photos, tables, or underlying project outputs into the app without item-specific rights confirmation.

limitations: The review is limited to the CvSU Research Center listing and searchable text of the January 2021 and September 2022 CvSU newsletters.
Absence of fish terms in public summaries does not establish that the full project omitted fish sampling.
The catalog and planning newsletter give different project periods; no final report was located to reconcile them.
No species-level, current-presence, absence, catchability, diet, safety, legal, or geometry claim is supported by this follow-up.
nextAction: Seek the final Imus project report and its deliverables through an authorized CvSU library/repository route; ask for the final project period, any fish-sampling methods and site/date/taxon table, voucher identifiers, and item-specific reuse terms. Keep the inquiry unsent unless separately authorized.
